# Package API, Declarations, and Migration Ledger

This page is generated from all 40 public manifests, package documentation, and
`governance/package-release-notes.json`. It records source candidates without
publishing them. CI rejects a version change unless its release classification,
summary, and migration guidance are updated at the same time.

The declaration targets below describe the packed manifest contract. The
package pages remain the human API and usage authority; generated declarations
and clean-consumer tests remain the executable type authority.

| `@bsv/402-pay`                    | `0.3.6`      | `0.3.6`  | none      | [API and usage](../packages/middleware/402-pay.md)                    | No API, wire or data migration is required. Redistributors must retain the included license and notice files. Custom clients must send a strictly framed BRC-95 Atomic BEEF envelope whose subject is the payment transaction; plain BEEF is no longer accepted. Legacy Atomic BEEF containing unrelated branches remains compatible because the server reduces it to the declared subject and dependency closure. The default replay store is bounded and process-local; production services with more than one serving process or node must inject the same durable atomic PaymentReplayStore everywhere. Low-level validators should retain one wallet object or pass an explicit store. Applications that relied on implicit console diagnostics must supply the optional structured logger. Treat an unchallenged 503 after payment submission as ambiguous and reconcile the transaction before requesting another payment. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with the package. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. Consumers may keep their current SDK or install @bsv/sdk 4.0.1; no migration is required for this package. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. | `@bsv/auth`                       | `0.1.9`      | `0.1.9`  | none      | [API and usage](../packages/middleware/auth.md)                       | No API, wire or data migration is required. Redistributors must retain the included license and notice files. No valid proof bytes or public API shape changes. Client and server must use the same protocol tuple; security levels 0, 1, and 2 remain supported and select wallet consent policy while the explicit counterparty scopes derivation at every level. Proof and wallet adapters must supply plain own data fields and dense byte arrays; inherited, accessor-backed, sparse, or malformed runtime shapes fail closed. Structured bodies containing non-finite numbers or negative zero must be normalized to an unambiguous wire representation before signing. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. Consumers may keep their current SDK or install @bsv/sdk 4.0.1; no migration is required for this package. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. | `@bsv/btms-permission-module`     | `1.2.5`      | `1.2.5`  | none      | [API and usage](../packages/wallet/btms-permission-module.md)         | No API, wire or data migration is required. Redistributors must retain the included license and notice files. Valid canonical BTMS flows remain compatible. Custom prompts must return literal true, authorization maps may contain at most 1,024 entries, and callers must provide dense signatures, safe exact totals, and canonical preimages; coercive or trailing-byte forms now fail closed. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. Consumers may keep their current SDK or install @bsv/sdk 4.0.1; no migration is required for this package. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. No API, codec, object identifier, service schema, or wire-format migration. Use @bsv/chirp 0.1.3 with SDK 2.8.9 or later and Cloud Bucket 0.2.48 or Lite 0.1.45 for authenticated binary uploads, including full 4 MiB chunks. Custom authenticated transports must send the supplied owned byte body unchanged and supply ordinary HTTP framing; Content-Type remains signed through AuthFetch. Earlier service entrypoints do not parse staged binary bytes before authentication and require this service patch. Existing stored objects, sessions, advertisements and leases remain unchanged. SDK consumers may retain ^2.4.1 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. Consumers may keep their current SDK or install @bsv/sdk 4.0.1; no migration is required for this package. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. | `@bsv/color-permission-module`    | `0.2.2`      | `0.2.2`  | none      | [API and usage](../packages/wallet/color-permission-module.md)        | 0.1.1 restores numeric module balance queries for established clients. Wallet hosts use SDK4.0.1 or newer and register the color scheme with the underlying wallet, a ColorOverlayProvider and a prompt callback. Exact accounting and value movement enumerate outputs; numeric summaries above 2^53 may round. Published inventory scope and wallet data remain unchanged. 0.2.0: No migration for hosts that register no profiles: behaviour is 0.1.1's (numeric balances, SDK ^4.0.1, #1338 suffix tags and inputBEEF recovery). ColorOverlayProvider.submit receives an optional third offChainValues argument; existing providers ignore it. Hosts that register profiles must supply a durable ColorModuleStore, submit plain-noSend hand-overs and pending receipts themselves, and call markSettled(txid) once the overlay admitted them. For every host, each consent message now carries seekPermission and a declined request throws ColorConsentDeclinedError, whose message is the 0.1.0 text prefixed with [ColorConsentDeclinedError]. 0.1.1 advertised brc207-color=5; 0.2.0 advertises brc207-color=4, the discovery value the pinned BRC-207 revision defines, so apps that check for 4 discover the module. 0.2.1: no migration. 0.2.2: no migration. | `@bsv/ecpm-permission-module`     | `0.2.0`      | `0.2.0`  | none      | [API and usage](../packages/wallet/ecpm-permission-module.md)         | Breaking. Every ECPM scalar changes, under every counterparty including self, so a point masked with 0.1.x cannot be unmasked with 0.2.0. Finish or restart any in-progress protocol on one version, and do not mix versions among participants. Request arguments, result format, permission prompts, cached-grant scope and peer ranges are unchanged. Hosts that call dispose during an in-flight request now receive a closed request instead of a late result. Other BRC-229 implementations must adopt the amended canonical scalar derivation and its new conformance vectors. Redistributors must retain the included license and notice files. No migration is required: this is the package's first appearance in ts-stack and it has not been published to npm before. Consumers supply their own wallet, storage and transport. @bsv/sdk is a required peer dependency. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. 0.2.0: No migration is required. Every change is additive over the published 0.1.1 and no export was removed, narrowed or renamed. A host that invented its own message id may keep it, but two hosts interoperate only on the derived id. The widened KeyPackage lifetime is read from the same notBefore and notAfter fields a 0.1.x peer already validates, so 0.1.x and 0.2.0 members interoperate in both directions with no wire, persistence or data migration. The templates are new files reachable through ./templates/*; nothing imports them unless a host asks for them. | `@bsv/lch`                        | `0.3.1`      | `0.3.1`  | none      | [API and usage](../packages/content/lch.md)                           | No API, wire or data migration is required. Redistributors must retain the included license and notice files. Replace buyer.quote(endpoint, request, issuer, keyGrants) with buyer.quote(verifiedSignedOffer, request, expectedSeller, keyGrants). JavaScript callers that still pass an endpoint string fail before transport I/O. Persist the returned plan and every partial settlement proof, retry with the same funded transaction, and configure a profile-aware agreementEvaluator before completion or recovery. Low-level unverified recovery results must not authorize key storage or content access. DNS endpoints require an address-pinning connector outside trusted browser environments. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md with the package; published BRC-170 remains authoritative if the implementation and standard differ. SDK consumers may retain ^2.4.1 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. The optional overlay-acquisition and overlay-covenant entries require the coordinated SDK3.3.0 output and revenue-listing companions; existing root peer ranges remain unchanged. Ordinary BRC-170 imports and SDK2 consumers remain unchanged. Decoded acquisition context and entitlement fingerprints remain explicitly unverified. Opt-in callers must install local proof sources and protected immutable-object custody before funding. LCHOverlayPaidDomain performs the concrete fixed-render/direct-collector checks; unsupported policy terms and profiles fail before funding. Ordinary BRC-170 imports, CORE_CAPABILITIES and SDK2 peers stay unchanged. The minor candidate adds APIs and a locally qualified authenticated native paid-lookup recovery flow. The current native covenant acquisition reference examples are implemented; their selectors and complete final-source gates are recorded in the checkpoint inventory. The browser workbench separately demonstrates progressive and live lookup. Install LCHOverlayPaidSeller only with the protected coordinator, actual read-only native credit reconciliation and complete original CEKs; financial effects remain owned by the coordinator and native adapters. Opt-in covenant callers must compose the terms adapter with actual complete genesis/Script/purchase, role and release verification; terms validation alone cannot issue a License or authorize decryption. Preserve the buyer-free standing Offer and exact original signed Request on every retry. Import LCHOverlayCovenantDomain through @bsv/lch/overlay-covenant, reserve original and positive-verification custody before financial work, and install actual full lineage/purchase/release proof ports. A decoded portable package, signed settlement or entitlement fingerprint alone cannot authorize playback. Public disclosed native fixtures compose the current covenant, encrypted custody, native wallet, seller and authenticated admission/recovery; full checkpoint qualification remains required. Install LCHOverlayCovenantSeller with actual full verifiers and the protected purchase coordinator; the advertised finite request/response limits must reserve the complete future C context before preparation. Issuance requires the complete retained candidate passed by the current coordinator, independently assessed release and original private material. Catalogue withdrawal does not replace that obligation. Combined wallet-backed topical-admission and native reference demonstrations are implemented; complete final-source qualification remains required. The opt-in covenant domain accepts complete plain BEEF selected by the original explicit wallet txid, independent of proof-record order; present Atomic BEEF markers must match. All original independent material, Script, lineage and licence checks remain. Ordinary BRC-170 behavior and persisted formats are unchanged. Existing BRC170 and paid-lookup behavior is unchanged. The approved pre-adoption C profile replacement requires purchaseCommitment in its signed settlement and in installed purchase verifier results; return the full authenticated input-zero SHA256d digest with an owned synchronous checkCurrent guard. Never infer it from equal outputs or transport claims. Preserve original signed release, License, settlement and protected obligations; currentAlias is separate unverified transport evidence. Qualify the replacement family, immutable collector terms, protected child wallet and native alias custody before advertising C. No existing ordinary content or paid-lookup stored format is reinterpreted. For current C representation, select decodeLCHCollectorRevenueProfile/bindLCHCollectorRevenueProfile and supply the exact immutable schedule and expiryHeight. New preparations require independently verified active stage and installed current height below expiry; retained obligations do not repeat that new-work predicate. These helpers do not authenticate Offers, verify ancestry/currentness or migrate historical owners; the current reference composition installs those independent responsibilities explicitly. Authenticate current C with validateLCHOverlayCovenantProfileTerms and retain its original consent; validateLCHOverlayCovenantProfilePromise validates a frozen obligation, while validateLCHOverlayCovenantProfileWindow is for new work. Independently verify authorized current-family lineage, roles, active stage and installed chain height before financial work. These terms interfaces perform no wallet action and do not migrate the historical buyer/seller/native alias owners. Select decodeLCHOverlayCovenantProfilePurchaseEvidence and bindLCHOverlayCovenantProfileSettlement for the current immutable descriptor. Representation and signed commitment binding do not establish actual Bitcoin history, Script execution, roles, release satisfaction, License validity or native alias ownership; retain independent full verification and historical entitlement checks. Select LCHOverlayCovenantProfileDomain for the current immutable collector. Initialize protected custody and retain/recheck fundingPreflight immediately before financial effects. Install actual complete current lineage, original funded and released transaction proof, and release-policy ports. Existing historical domain IDs/formats/defaults remain unchanged; retained delivery and offline playback never repeat a new-funding expiry predicate. The current reference composition separately installs native alias/action custody and the current seller; neither responsibility is supplied by the buyer domain alone. Select LCHOverlayCovenantProfileSeller for current immutable seller material. Its distinct installation identity does not reinterpret historical custody. Supply complete actual reserve/activation/purchase/release verifiers; retain and recheck the preparation guard before promising material. Original historical seller interfaces/IDs/formats/defaults remain. The current reference composition separately installs coordinator commitment packets and native alias/action/admission/HTTP owners; the seller domain alone supplies none of those authorities. Omit verification.candidate to preserve the prior installation identity and absent binding capability. Installing it selects a distinct full-commitment domain before buyer creation or reopen; its verification ID must bind complete independently selected algorithms. Provide the full ProfilePurchase verifier and same-context guard, retain original protected custody, and assess current alias placement separately on the buyer's own chain. Historical new-funding cutoffs do not re-gate this read-only verification. These additive components remain under native, packed and platform qualification; no full checkpoint claim. Conforming dense integer-byte wallet results remain compatible. Custom wallet adapters must return every plaintext/ciphertext byte as an own data value; missing or accessor-backed bytes fail with ERR_LCH_KEY rather than being synthesized. The additive seller assessment companion retains pending-finality or pending-evidence before financial reservation. Installing verification.assessPurchase selects a distinct material binding. Complete original consent, roles, Script/domain and release checks remain mandatory; pending evidence cannot fulfill compensation or issue a License. Consumers may keep their current SDK or install @bsv/sdk 4.0.1; no migration is required for this package. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. | `@bsv/output-knowledge`           | `0.1.1`      | `0.1.1`  | none      | [API and usage](../packages/application/output-knowledge.md)          | No API, wire or data migration is required. Redistributors must retain the included license and notice files. New opt-in package requiring SDK ^3.3.0, which introduces the output-protocol APIs; SDK3.0–3.2 do not provide these APIs. Preserve wallet custody and explicit action authorization; do not infer spending from source membership changes. New journals seal configured currentness rules in local frame v3 with canonical assessment ordering. Existing v1/v2 journals retain their encoding and replay behavior when read or extended. Adopting v3 for an older journal or changing policies requires a new namespace; retain the old journal for audit and recovery. Body-only proposal journal entries retain their bytes and retry keys. Upgrade all SQLite proposal writers before relying on reserved completion capacity; capacity limits are sealed, and older pending jobs do not gain retroactive guarantees. ProposalService requires durable context/capacity storage, an authenticated transport, a current host access policy and idempotent durable topic admission. SDKProposalEvidence verifies exact BEEF/Script against an installed immutable chain view; it does not replace topic rules or establish unspentness. Legacy proposal-service/1 records remain readable; rich evidence reservations use local proposal-service/2, so upgrade readers before writing v2. Context-required admission cannot synthesize missing legacy material. Reservation verification and actual durable topic assessment remain distinct. Import workflow control storage from ./operations or ./operations/sqlite. These local CAS cells do not replace receipt journals or validate protocol transitions. Use explicit create only for new workflow identities; recover existing storage with open, and treat absence as lost state. Existing exports and journal formats remain unchanged. Import the live adapter from ./sources/live-lookup. Create its durable control cell once before network I/O, recover that exact cell after restart, and reuse the source instance across cancelled or uncertain connection attempts. Its local control format is output-live-lookup-source/1. Lost continuity requires an explicit new source generation; a local reset never manufactures a successful cursor or Bitcoin spend. Existing finite adapters and their browser entry are unchanged. Import the optional revenue-listing entry explicitly and supply the authenticated fixed program plus an installed immutable chain view. Its historical verdict does not establish asset authority, currentness, acquisition association or private fulfillment. No existing root export, wire format or journal migration. The optional revenue-listing authority port requires explicit dedicated key custody and installed consent policy; it never extracts a wallet funding root key or substitutes BRC-100 derived identities. Its signature checks do not establish full-transaction validity, lineage or fulfillment, and it introduces no existing stored-format migration. Root storage is opt-in through root-eviction types and root-eviction/sqlite. Explicit creation uses a new database file; recovery never creates missing state or changes its sealed identity, chain or capacities. All service instances and serving adapters must share the same durable gate. The journal does not install requester authority, validate advertisement BEEF/Script, implement broader bans or expiry scheduling, or mount HTTP handlers. Current authorization, evidence policy, index integration and final middleware enqueue qualification remain service responsibilities; do not advertise the full BRC-199 profile from this component alone. Import SDKRootEvictionEvidence from root-eviction/evidence with an installed immutable chain resolver and owned verification context. Its verified facts do not authorize suppression/restoration or establish currentness, and operator references are not fetched or automatically authorized. No existing wire or stored-format migration. Existing deterministic root methods and stored format remain unchanged. The optional RootEvictionCheckedStorage companion requires synchronous trusted clock/access/context callbacks that share the same physical gate or an independently coherent local port. Retain the returned observed head through signing and recheck it at final enqueue. These methods do not install network authentication, chain currentness or operator policy. RootEvictionContracts requires the original retained selector on recovery. Its record must be persisted atomically with first intake; the portable helper does not itself store that record; use the optional coordinated journal for atomic intake. RootEvictionCoordinatedStorage is an optional companion. Existing configurations retain exact root-eviction/1 behavior. New coordination configurations use root-eviction/2 and a sealed bounded original-contract byte capacity; upgrade existing files only through upgradeCoordination with the same root, chain and prior capacities. Already-open old connections fail after upgrade. Preserve backups and all history; missing legacy selections remain unavailable and cannot be invented from current discovery. HTTP, broader local bans, scheduling and all serving adapters remain separate requirements. SQLiteRootEvictionMaintenance opens an existing root journal with its exact sealed configuration; no new format or implicit creation. Install synchronous root-maintenance authorization and a trusted clock. Schedule bounded startup and periodic scan passes, restarting without a cursor at each pass end. Maintenance does not grant requester status access, process peer decisions or restore eligibility. RootEvictionRecoveryStorage preserves existing interfaces and formats. Authorize its worker guard independently of requester status access; missing original selections remain unavailable. Run maintenance expiry even when current chain/context checks prevent richer recovery. New service installations pass strictly decoded received UTF-8 text and an available manifest snapshot; third-party coordinated adapters implement its text-intake contract. Returned observations still require the native final-enqueue revision and current-access guard. Existing parsed packet calls and lookup defaults remain unchanged. RootEvictionScheduler is opt-in and defaults to manual/advisory expiry. Use maintenance and recovery ports for the same sealed journal; install automatic policy and guarded authority explicitly. Observe its lifetime and reports, stop intake and await physical drain before closing injected storage. No existing interface, stored format or default route changes. SQLiteRootEvictionLocalRules requires coordination plus explicit localRules configuration. Preserve formats1/2; upgrade format2 only with upgradeLocalRules, preserving exact prior capacities and fencing older connections. Install trusted rule evaluation and operator attribution separately, report unknown results as null and complete projection before serving. Local active rules reserve future lift records/epochs/revisions; permanent history is never silently reclaimed. The optional evidence entry adds SDKRootAdvertisementEvidence; the existing signed-request verifier and its authority checks remain compatible. Existing proposal journal bytes and methods are unchanged. Opt into responseEnqueue only with a transport guard that runs after signing and supplies exact response/record, original-contract, retention and current-access validation. All authorization writers require the same gate or explicit coherence; callbacks are synchronous and cannot reenter. Responses are bounded to 4 MiB, with smaller selected-contract limits enforced by disclosure. Track actual enqueue independently: a subsequent error cannot undo delivery or authorize a replacement response. The new ProposalResponseDisclosure companion is opt-in and runs with ProposalJournalSend after signing; current host access must share its policy domain. Retrying an older recorded publication returns its original acknowledgement without replacing the current head; no stored-format migration. Existing journal constructor behavior is preserved. Use create only for intentional installation and open for restart; missing sealed state fails rather than resetting the namespace. Observe the optional scheduler lifetime and drain stop before closing dependencies. These additions neither compact terminal fences nor initiate new finalizations. No existing schema, wire or default behavior migration. Opt in with the same sessions/contracts/current authorization and an explicit synchronous control policy. All relevant writers must share the durable guard protocol; native callbacks cannot await, close or reenter storage. Existing workers may omit nextInvalidation. Installed deadline hooks must be pure and paired with durable invalidation in advance; applications still retire previously displayed activity at its deadline. Existing expired-assessment behavior and stored/wire formats remain unchanged. Await setContext before treating a new verification context as committed; flush does not complete a pending context write. No new wire or storage migration. Use a new journal namespace when enabling proposal acceptance or changing its reader/source/policy installation. Existing default local frames and unaccepted proposal-group behavior remain unchanged; no implicit upgrade or downgrade. Install same-name source/proposal services under the existing observation contract. Authenticated proposal heads are signed variants, not a current-channel selection; provider states remain reports and do not authorize Bitcoin or application effects. A separately registered query/projection and current private authorization remain necessary. Existing stores may omit the new pure reducer deadline hook; a due hook requires durable worker invalidation before reads, including historical publication. The runtime permits one bounded recovery when expiry crosses after worker return. The SQLite journal/index refactor preserves existing constructors, namespace formats and default behavior. Internal shared transaction and savepoint domains coordinate SQL with staged journal caches; they are not public raw-SQL or authorization ports. Independently opened adapters are not atomic compound writers. Failed rollback retires uncertain connections; preserve the original operation for durable recovery. The shared primitive alone does not enable the optional compound profile. Install the query and exact source/reader policy explicitly; wrap an already connected durable BRC103 live source and project only published core input. Current intent does not establish complete history or effect authority. Legacy manual views lack required order/generation facts. Empty completed generations retire prior state. Select the separately sealed compound owner explicitly; the client components do not install it automatically. Import the Node-only factory from ./proposals/channels-sqlite. Initial create is atomic; recovery open requires all original components and sealed limits. Route every producer through its journal or bounded batch commit, and use its feed/sessions for lookup. Fresh authorization must include the mandatory policy visibility guard returned by authorizeLookup, in addition to current host access guards. A pure optional readVisibility descriptor preserves read continuity only when equal values mean identical permissions for every principal; omitted hooks conservatively compare the full signed body. No standalone format migration or automatic compaction is introduced. Retain all service-identity history and fences when capacity is exhausted. The transient signature cache retains no payloads or durable decisions; no wire or storage migration is needed. The protected ledger requires explicit exclusive creation, stable external store identity/custody and consistent whole-database/key backup. It has no remote mutation endpoint or automatic initialization/compaction; complete qualification of the publication and acquisition compositions remains required. The in-memory root signature cache changes no persisted or wire format. Preserve the authoritative private database and its separate indexing/encryption custody; opening never creates replacement state. No existing application behavior changes. The private lineage implementation extraction requires no consumer, wire or storage migration; existing revenue-listing imports and verification decisions are unchanged. Existing private storage calls and version-1 records retain their behavior. Verified staging is an explicit optional installation and uses version-2 fences with the original contract; missing legacy context requires explicit reconciliation. The optional Node private publication entry requires an explicitly created or reopened seller/chain domain, protected custody, installed domain validation and current access/chain policy. Existing ordinary imports, two-argument publication storage and version-1 fences retain their behavior. Metadata-backed unavailable status preserves original obligations and never recreates material; restoration is explicit. Drain reconciliation and physical coordinator work before closing custody. HTTP publication remains separate from private lookup acquisition and purchase release. The paid-acquisition composition preserves existing stored formats and commits funding fences with progress atomically. Original quote/material ownership, wallet recovery, release policy and guarded HTTP delivery are coordinated through the installed private/node service. The native acquisition owner adds no migration of existing stored formats. | `@bsv/overlay-topics`             | `2.0.4`      | `2.0.4`  | none      | [API and usage](../packages/overlays/overlay-topics.md)               | Topics2 is a breaking retirement candidate. Remove DIDTopicManager/createDIDLookupService/DIDRecord/DIDQuery and tm_did/ls_did usage. Resolve immutable identity-key DIDs offline; explicitly configured tm_identity/ls_identity supplies certificate discovery, not DID-document mutation or automatic trust. Preserve existing database/history and plan service rollout without automatic replacement installation. See docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. Mandala is a clean break with no data migration: the old MandalaToken/MandalaAdmin wire format is no longer admitted and 1.x Mandala rows are not read or converted, so start Mandala on a new database with new deploys (existing on-chain outputs are not spent or deleted). MandalaTopicManager drops adminWallet, adminProtocolID and stateStore.isAdminOutpoint and requires trustedIssuers (non-empty compressed lowercase public keys) and engineOutputs, with optional membership, membershipExempt and onOwnerRepair; pass the same MandalaStorageManager (a MandalaStateStore) to admission and lookup. Refusals are MandalaReject { code, reason } from the Reasons catalog; do not match on old error text. MandalaLinkagePayload is replaced by MandalaEnvelope with encodeEnvelope/decodeEnvelope; the register action is replaced by a deploy at output 0 with a deploySig. foldAction, defaultAssetState, AssetAdminState, FoldContext and MandalaTokenRecord use tokenId (<txid>_0) instead of assetId, drop issuerIdentityKey and add feeRatePerKb. Persisted schema (section 6.6): new mandalaOwners and mandalaAuthorities collections; mandalaTokens, mandalaMetadata, mandalaAssetStates and mandalaAdminHistory are keyed by tokenId, metadata holds the decoded deploy payload, and history rows store kind, detailsHex, commitment and delta (plus optional frozenAmount/frozenOwner on freezes). De-trusting an issuer key revokes the authority coins it holds; rotate keys by moving authority coins first. Operators register tm_mandala_registry/ls_mandala_registry explicitly. The infra/overlay-server wiring follows after publication (P1b). The prior 2.0.0 contracts above are the published baseline. This 2.0.1 UMP patch has no API, wire or schema migration; deploy with overlay 2.6.4 to retain history past confirmation. Consumers may keep their current SDK or install @bsv/sdk 4.0.1; no migration is required for this package. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. To restore larger KVStore tag sets end to end, deploy this package together with SDK4.1.1 and upgrade client SDKs. No KVStore database or token migration is required; preserve all existing tags and signed bytes. Per-tag validation, overall payload/request bounds, signatures, controller binding and pagination are unchanged. Embedded certificate requests: no API break and empty answers stay off by default. toPeer on a session whose embedded certificate answer is pending can be delayed, at most 30 seconds, by the wallet's certificate lookup; a send from inside a certificates-received listener is not held. Enable sendEmptyCertificateResponses only for servers that accept an empty answer: @bsv/auth-express-middleware replies 400 ERR_CERTIFICATES_REQUIRED and clears that session's active certificate request. go-sdk's Peer already sends empty answers and accepts them. LivePolicy endpoint: no consumer migration is required; both options are optional and the default endpoint, client, cache and fallback rate are unchanged. To use another network, pass a configured LivePolicy to Transaction.fee() instead of relying on the default. Whole-BEEF lookups: no API, wire or data migration; the default is unchanged and callers opt in per query. A lookup service answering whole-BEEF queries with plain BEEF should put each output's subject last; callers that need the longest history from several hosts merge the onEvidence copies themselves. SignedMessage: no consumer migration is required. signWithWallet and the expectedSigner option are additive, and three-argument verify calls behave as before. A caller that passes expectedSigner gets false, not a thrown error, for a designated-verifier signature by another key even when the recipient key is missing or wrong. Zero-field certificate proofs: existing validateCertificates callers keep the nonempty path unless they pass allowZeroFields true, which they should do only for a request they retained locally and bound to an authenticated message. A zero-field proof carries no keyring for the verifier and the initial-response signature does not cover certificates, so it shows that a valid certificate names the authenticated identity as subject, not that the holder presented it; do not call decryptFields on such a certificate. Behaviour change on the nonempty path: a session whose store lost its request snapshot no longer freezes a policy at authentication time, so later standalone certificate responses on that session are checked against the Peer's current certificatesToRequest. No API break, wire or stored-data change. No consumer migration is required. No consumer migration is required. No consumer migration is required. Behaviour change: a 2xx body reporting a status in ARC's failure set (REJECTED, DOUBLE_SPEND_ATTEMPTED, INVALID, MALFORMED, MINED_IN_STALE_BLOCK), a txStatus naming an orphan, or another well-formed txid is now a failure, with code txStatus and more { txStatus, arcStatus, competingTxs } (or ERR_TXID_MISMATCH). Callers that treated every 2xx Teranode answer as success must handle that failure result. Callers that need certainty for RECEIVED check txStatus or poll the service (GET /tx/{txid}). No consumer migration is required. | `@bsv/simple`                     | `0.7.3`      | `0.7.3`  | none      | [API and usage](../packages/helpers/simple.md)                        | No API, wire or data migration is required. Redistributors must retain the included license and notice files. Simple0.7 is a breaking pre-1.0 candidate. Remove mutable DID/resolver/provider configuration, proxy handlers and DIDError/types; use DID.fromIdentityKey/resolve and wallet.getDID. CredentialIssuer.issue returns {credential,keyringForSubject}; verify accepts exact JSON or UTF8 bytes and returns structured cryptographic results. The HTTP verify route now requires {credential: originalEnvelopeJson} with original text as a string; parsed objects return HTTP400. Web request decoding rejects duplicate members and invalid UTF8, and custom parsed-body adapters must establish equivalent strict decoding. Preserve received text and inspect verification.verified, not HTTP success. Local revocation record status is retained/unknown, not inferred chain revocation. See docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. Replace createServerWalletHandler() deployments with createServerWalletHandler({ authorize: async ({ action, headers }) => authenticatedSessionCanUseAction(headers, action) }). The callback must return literal true for each status, create, request, receive, balance, outputs, or reset action; omission now returns HTTP 403 for every action. Roll out the authentication layer and callback with the package, update anonymous probes or automation, and apply the same policy to every replica. Do not emulate the old public behavior with an unconditional authorize: () => true callback. Valid recipient derivations and authenticated Message Box peers remain supported; malformed, wrong-owner, or transaction-mutated flows now fail closed. New CredentialSchema and Certifier records use canonical 32-byte types. Current SDK wallet methods reject historical short types, so do not put migration aliases in wallet list, acquire, prove, or relinquish calls. Export affected records through the storage version that created them, authenticate them offline against the exact locally configured identifier, and reissue/import canonical replacements; no legacy certificate is rewritten automatically. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/. Persisted local field ordering requires no migration; transport adapters preserve original certificate signing bytes. Consumers may keep their current SDK or install @bsv/sdk 4.0.1; no migration is required for this package. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. Consumers may keep their current SDK or install @bsv/sdk 4.0.1; no migration is required for this package. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. | `@bsv/verifast`                   | `0.3.10`     | `0.3.10` | none      | [API and usage](../packages/sdk/verifast.md)                          | No API, wire or data migration is required. Redistributors must retain the included license and notice files. Valid typed verification calls and worker protocols remain compatible. Custom module factories and WASM adapters must return the exact documented binary and boolean shapes; coercive network, height, flag, byte, batch, verdict, lifecycle, or disposed-instance values now fail closed. Keep THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with every JavaScript and WebAssembly distribution. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.8 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. Consumers may keep their current SDK or install @bsv/sdk 4.0.1; no migration is required for this package. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. | `@bsv/wallet-helper`              | `0.2.0`      | `0.2.0`  | none      | [API and usage](../packages/helpers/wallet-helper.md)                 | No API, wire or data migration is required. Redistributors must retain the included license and notice files. getAddress now derives with forSelf: true and returns the caller-owned side of the bilateral relationship. Applications that stored or coordinated the previous peer-owned result must regenerate and exchange the corrected address before sending value. Amount must be an integer from 1 through 1,000 and counterparties must be valid public keys. Valid canonical transaction-builder flows remain supported; malformed, ambiguous, or wallet-mutated results now fail closed. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with the package. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. Consumers may keep their current SDK or install @bsv/sdk 4.0.1; no migration is required for this package. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. 0.2.0: no migration is required; transactions built without tags or labels produce the same createAction arguments as 0.1.12. | `@bsv/wallet-relay`               | `0.8.0`      | `0.8.0`  | none      | [API and usage](../packages/wallet/wallet-relay.md)                   | No consumer migration is required. Handlers that return getSession() unchanged include topic and protocolID automatically. A handler that rebuilds the JSON must copy topic, backendIdentityKey, and protocolID from that object: topic equals the QR topic, backendIdentityKey equals the QR key, and protocolID equals the QR's canonical protocol JSON string. Wallets that ignore unknown fields keep working. A session response that carries a malformed topic or protocolID now fails validateSessionInfo, so WalletRelayClient rejects it. No API migration is required for allowLocalNetworkHttp: the default transport policy is unchanged, except that all of 127.0.0.0/8 and, on the mobile pairing boundary, *.localhost now count as loopback. To pair a phone with a development backend on a LAN IP address, set allowLocalNetworkHttp: true on WalletRelayService, on WalletRelayClient or useWalletRelayClient, and in the wallet's parsePairingUri and WalletPairingSession calls, for example behind a developer setting; a wallet without it rejects such QR codes. Never enable it in production: an on-path attacker can rewrite the plaintext session lookup and relay URL of an HTTP origin. The WalletPairingSession and WalletRelayClient transport errors are reworded to 'Pairing origin must be HTTPS, except for loopback development' and 'Relay API URL requires HTTPS, except for loopback development.', and a server or desktop private-network rejection names allowLocalNetworkHttp; callers that matched the previous text must update the match. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. | `@bsv/wallet-toolbox`             | `2.18.0`     | `2.18.1` | patch     | [API and usage](../packages/wallet/wallet-toolbox.md)                 | No consumer migration is required. No consumer migration is required. Exports, types, storage and wire formats are unchanged. An application that passed seekPermission: false and relied on the prompt appearing anyway now receives the existing seekPermission=false error and should omit the flag or pass true to allow the prompt. No API, wire or schema migration. Height acceptance widens by one block; time-lock acceptance follows median time past, usually about an hour behind the wall clock. No API, wire or schema migration. A new process sweeps once at its first processed header, then once per triggerMsecs (one day by default). No API, wire or schema migration. The ordinary createAction path runs in Storage, so upgrade a remote Storage server for it; the action batch path is fixed by upgrading the wallet host. No consumer migration is required. | `create-bsv-app`                  | `1.2.1`      | `1.3.0`  | minor     | [API and usage](../packages/helpers/create-bsv-app.md)                | No consumer migration is required. Existing projects keep their dependency ranges until the next add-mode run, which merges the manifest's capabilities (tx-core included) and raises outdated ranges. devDependencies and unrecognised ranges are never changed and are listed for manual review. An add-mode run that selects a capability without what it requires now also writes the required capability's files and dependencies and records it; existing files are still skipped unless --force is given. Add-mode --file configs no longer drop the manifest's recorded capabilities, so they need not repeat them; keys such a config leaves out (network, bsvDir, stack, targets, name) now come from the manifest instead of resetting to defaults. A project with no detectable frontend or backend must declare its stack (for example --frontend react, or a stack in the --file config) before capabilities can be added. `none` means the source manifest matches the recorded npm baseline. Any other
value records source ahead of that baseline; it does not establish the current
registry state. `initial` with a null published baseline identifies a new
package with no recorded published baseline; it does not invent an npm version or
waive publication checks. Publication, tags, releases, registry reconciliation,
and infrastructure dependency synchronization remain separate,
explicitly authorized operations.

## Package entry points

## @bsv/402-pay

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/middleware/402-pay.md](../packages/middleware/402-pay.md)
- Source: [packages/middleware/402-pay](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/middleware/402-pay)
- Release note: 0.3.6: Refreshes packed Apache-2.0 license, notice, patent and incorporated-material attribution files. The package includes the reviewed Apache-2.0 license, patent notice and incorporated-material notices. Adds an exact-tarball Vite and esbuild contract for the browser-safe client entry point, including a bundle-size ratchet and an assertion that server exports never leak into browser consumers. Retains the hash-pinned pre-uniformization Open BSV License version 4 grant as a scoped continuity notice. Standardizes first-party author metadata on the current BSV Association name. Binds BRC-121 pricing and internalization to the transaction declared by the BRC-95 Atomic BEEF subject, removes unrelated included branches, rejects trailing bytes and non-atomic envelopes, and requires affirmative wallet acceptance before serving paid content. Adds independent bounded atomic transaction replay claims so conforming BRC-100 wallets that omit the non-public isMerge detail cannot authorize duplicate access, preserves actual overpayments in middleware receipts, uses fixed bounded wallet descriptions, makes diagnostics opt-in, and returns an unchallenged 503 after ambiguous wallet or replay-store failures to avoid inducing a second spend. Aligns the development-only Vitest runner and V8 coverage provider at 4.1.11. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 lower bound; clean packed SDK2.8.11 and SDK3 candidate consumers are documented in the identity/DID/VC migration guide. Adds an SDK4 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 and SDK3 ranges. Requires the repaired SDK4.0.1 hotfix for the SDK4 peer alternative while retaining every existing SDK2/3 alternative and lower bound.
- Migration: No API, wire or data migration is required. Redistributors must retain the included license and notice files. Custom clients must send a strictly framed BRC-95 Atomic BEEF envelope whose subject is the payment transaction; plain BEEF is no longer accepted. Legacy Atomic BEEF containing unrelated branches remains compatible because the server reduces it to the declared subject and dependency closure. The default replay store is bounded and process-local; production services with more than one serving process or node must inject the same durable atomic PaymentReplayStore everywhere. Low-level validators should retain one wallet object or pass an explicit store. Applications that relied on implicit console diagnostics must supply the optional structured logger. Treat an unchallenged 503 after payment submission as ambiguous and reconcile the transaction before requesting another payment. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with the package. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. - Release note: Introduces the BRC-207 color wallet module for BRC-162 fungible tokens: receipt verification against the asset overlay, token sends funded from per-asset baskets with token change and signed during signAction, BRC-177 handoffs with an exact-amount split, a p color tag holding the SHA-256 of the derivation suffix on every output it files, inputBEEF for the token inputs the module selects (merged with the caller's, read by suffix tag in one listing per asset basket or bounded pagination when distinct payments share a suffix), input records bound to the action reference between createAction and signAction so signing does not list the wallet's outputs, createSignature for app-built transactions, and the p color assets and p color balance views. Assets first deployed as BRC-161 JSON, at any output index, are handled in BRC-162 form. 0.2.0 builds on the published 0.1.1 and includes all of its fixes: numeric p color balance summaries (summed exactly as a bigint, then one Number conversion), the unchanged inventory view (every held output, reserved ones listed with spendable false and color_state_reserved), the #1338 suffix tags and input BEEF recovery (outputs filed without a suffix tag are not selected or spendable through the module) and the SDK ^4.0.1 peer floor. 0.2.0 adds required processing profiles: a fail-closed handler registry (profiles option, with a required durable ColorModuleStore under color.v1. keys) in which every required profile must be registered with its version and handlers only restrict. Their hooks check descriptors and ext, route each asset to its own overlay provider, resolve unknown deploys, restrict holder operations, check plan profileData, supply BRC-22 submission data (passed to ColorOverlayProvider.submit as an optional third offChainValues argument) and, through admitReceipt, decide each receipt of their asset as settled or pending in place of the overlay spendability check. A pending receipt and the token change of a plain-noSend hand-over (sendPolicy plain-nosend: noSend required, change kept in the transaction, never submitted by the module) are tagged color_offline in the views until the host calls the in-process markSettled(txid), which is not a BRC-100 method. Receipts carry BRC-207 custody instructions only: any receipt profileData is rejected with the 0.1.0 error and the 1000-byte limit holds. actionConsent and transactionConsent take the token reader (and actionConsent the hand-over flag) in a trailing options object (ActionConsentOptions, TransactionConsentOptions); their 0.1.0 calls are unchanged. New error classes ProfileParamsError, ProfileDataError and ColorConsentDeclinedError carry a [ClassName] message prefix, and every consent message carries seekPermission. Plans also cover deploys, mints, burns and authority operations. Module-built deploys that require profiles, BRC-161 JSON outputs held by the wallet, BRC-209, and createSignature for assets whose profiles define sendPolicy, submissionData or checkPlanData fail explicitly in this version, as does a plain-noSend hand-over signed with options.noSend false or a sendWith batch. The module advertises brc207-color=4, the BRC-207 revision it implements. The pending balance (p color balance with tags ['color_offline']) is a number in totalOutputs, like every balance; color_offline outputs stay listed in the inventory with their computed color_state tag. The browser budget is 0.1.1's (Vite raw/gzip/brotli 1375000/345000/270000, esbuild 1060000/310000/255000 bytes), which covers the measured 0.2.0 bundle (Vite 1281058/317875/251521, esbuild 989064/288967/234125). 0.2.1: the p color <hex> tag value is 32 random bytes drawn per output instead of the SHA-256 of the derivation suffix, and a caller-supplied tag of that form is dropped; the stored form is unchanged. 0.2.2: the p color assets inventory and the explicit-input check read the basket-prefix listing with limit 10,000, the listing cap, instead of the default of ten; while an action batch was open, the wallet cut that listing to ten outputs, so the inventory showed at most ten and an owned eleventh input was treated as foreign.
- Migration: 0.1.1 restores numeric module balance queries for established clients. Wallet hosts use SDK4.0.1 or newer and register the color scheme with the underlying wallet, a ColorOverlayProvider and a prompt callback. Exact accounting and value movement enumerate outputs; numeric summaries above 2^53 may round. Published inventory scope and wallet data remain unchanged. 0.2.0: No migration for hosts that register no profiles: behaviour is 0.1.1's (numeric balances, SDK ^4.0.1, #1338 suffix tags and inputBEEF recovery). ColorOverlayProvider.submit receives an optional third offChainValues argument; existing providers ignore it. Hosts that register profiles must supply a durable ColorModuleStore, submit plain-noSend hand-overs and pending receipts themselves, and call markSettled(txid) once the overlay admitted them. For every host, each consent message now carries seekPermission and a declined request throws ColorConsentDeclinedError, whose message is the 0.1.0 text prefixed with [ColorConsentDeclinedError]. 0.1.1 advertised brc207-color=5; 0.2.0 advertises brc207-color=4, the discovery value the pinned BRC-207 revision defines, so apps that check for 4 discover the module. 0.2.1: no migration. 0.2.2: no migration.

## @bsv/ecpm-permission-module

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/wallet/ecpm-permission-module.md](../packages/wallet/ecpm-permission-module.md)
- Source: [packages/wallet/ecpm-permission-module](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/wallet/ecpm-permission-module)
- Release note: 0.2.0 fixes GHSA-m3c6-3mv8-j86f. The module no longer multiplies the caller's point by the raw BRC-42/43 child key, which let a caller able to compute the BRC-42 offset recover the wallet's root ECDH shared secret with a third party, with no prompt at security level 0. The child key is now used only as HKDF-SHA256 input, and the multiplication scalar is 1 + (the 48-byte HKDF output mod (n - 1)). The same level-0 oracle also exposed the wallet's self shared secret, allowing recovery of self-derived symmetric and HMAC keys and decryption of self-encrypted data. Apply and remove still round-trip, and masks from different wallets still commute. Regression tests cover third-party, self and caller-held counterparty recovery attempts plus fixed conformance vectors. Disposal also invalidates in-flight authorization and privileged key-provider results, so a late approval cannot restore a cleared grant or complete a torn-down request.
- Migration: Breaking. Every ECPM scalar changes, under every counterparty including self, so a point masked with 0.1.x cannot be unmasked with 0.2.0. Finish or restart any in-progress protocol on one version, and do not mix versions among participants. Request arguments, result format, permission prompts, cached-grant scope and peer ranges are unchanged. Hosts that call dispose during an in-flight request now receive a closed request instead of a late result. Other BRC-229 implementations must adopt the amended canonical scalar derivation and its new conformance vectors.

## @bsv/group-messaging

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/messaging/group-messaging.md](../packages/messaging/group-messaging.md)
- Source: [packages/messaging/group-messaging](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/messaging/group-messaging)
- Release note: 0.1.1: Refreshes packed Apache-2.0 license, notice, patent and incorporated-material attribution files. The package includes the reviewed Apache-2.0 license, patent notice and incorporated-material notices. Initial migration into ts-stack of end-to-end encrypted group messaging for BRC-100 wallets, with MLS (RFC 9420) group state by way of ts-mls and each member's MLS credential bound to their wallet's secp256k1 identity so a peer cannot join under a name that is not theirs. Ships storage backends for Map, SQL and IndexedDB, and transport backends for an in-process hub and @bsv/message-box-client with optional live socket delivery over a polling backstop. The library opens no database and no network connection of its own beyond the socket a caller explicitly asks for, and never stores private KeyPackage material. Requires the repaired SDK4.0.1 hotfix for the SDK4 peer alternative while retaining every existing SDK2/3 alternative and lower bound. 0.2.0 builds on the published 0.1.1 and includes it. Adds messageIdOf: replyTo and a reaction reference always named an id the library did not define, so each host invented one and two hosts inventing differently did not interoperate. The id is the SHA-256 of the MLS application message bytes in lower-case hex, derived rather than chosen, so sender and recipients reach it independently; every send returns it, every message event carries it, and a send that did not get through carries it on the deliveryFailed event and on the BroadcastError it rejects with, including across a retry that fails again. Adds TransportService.onLiveStatus, forwarding what the backend live connection is doing; LiveStatus moves to the backend contract so a backend other than MessageBox can report it, is still exported from the MessageBox backend that declared it, and the connection phase is replayed to a handler that subscribes late. A delivered report describes one batch rather than the connection, so it is not what gets replayed and two identical ones are both reported; close() releases the live-status handlers on the backend and through TransportService alike. Widens a KeyPackage lifetime window by 300 seconds at each end: ts-mls runs the lifetime check unconditionally for a commit the caller is sending, so a peer whose clock ran ahead rejected an add outright with "Current time not within Lifetime", observed on two devices 162 seconds apart. Ships five templates under templates/ to read and copy rather than import, with no export subpath for them and templates/**tests** excluded from the artifact: client-lifecycle, sql-shelf, transcript, web-crypto-conformance and managed-invitations. They ship as source to copy and carry no compatibility promise.
- Migration: No API, wire or data migration is required. Redistributors must retain the included license and notice files. No migration is required: this is the package's first appearance in ts-stack and it has not been published to npm before. Consumers supply their own wallet, storage and transport. @bsv/sdk is a required peer dependency. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. 0.2.0: No migration is required. Every change is additive over the published 0.1.1 and no export was removed, narrowed or renamed. Reaction.reference, MessageContent.replyTo and the reference arguments to sendReply and sendReaction remain typed string, documented on each field as the id messageIdOf derives. A host that invented its own message id may keep it, but two hosts interoperate only on the derived id. The widened KeyPackage lifetime is read from the same notBefore and notAfter fields a 0.1.x peer already validates, so 0.1.x and 0.2.0 members interoperate in both directions with no wire, persistence or data migration. The templates are new files reachable through ./templates/*; nothing imports them unless a host asks for them.

## @bsv/message-box-client

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/messaging/message-box-client.md](../packages/messaging/message-box-client.md)
- Source: [packages/messaging/message-box-client](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/messaging/message-box-client)
- Release note: PaymentToken now keeps an optional, bounded note and paymail from an incoming MessageBox payment. note is text of at most 500 characters and 2,000 bytes with no control characters; paymail is a name@domain address of at most 254 bytes that `parsePaymail` in `@bsv/ts-paymail` accepts. An invalid value is dropped and the payment is still returned. The token keeps exactly its old shape when the sender sent neither. Both fields are unverified text chosen by the sender. A token that carries a sender field is still rejected.
- Migration: No migration required. note and paymail are optional and absent on older senders.

## @bsv/overlay

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/overlays/overlay.md](../packages/overlays/overlay.md)
- Source: [packages/overlays/overlay](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/overlays/overlay)
- Release note: Proof ingest now records a Merkle proof for a transaction a topic applied without storing any of its outputs (for example a spend accepted only for the coin it consumed), so its applied rows become proven and enter BRC-136 anchors instead of handleNewMerkleProof throwing and /arc-ingest answering 400. Stores an ancestor's Merkle proof when a descendant output's stored BEEF already ends at a proven transaction that spends the ancestor or a bound descendant of it, skipping that descendant instead of throwing and leaving the ancestor's proof unstored; a BEEF that carries the ancestor is updated as before and other incomplete BEEFs still fail without writing. Knex storage widens outputs.satoshis to a 64-bit integer on MySQL and Postgres, so an admitted output above 2,147,483,647 satoshis is stored exactly instead of being clamped (MySQL) or failing to insert after broadcast (Postgres).
- Migration: No consumer migration is required. No consumer migration is required. Run the new satoshis-width migration from KnexStorageMigrations (overlay-express runs them at start). MySQL and Postgres rewrite the outputs table to change the column type, and Postgres blocks reads and writes on it meanwhile. Outputs MySQL already clamped to 2,147,483,647 satoshis are not corrected. No API or wire change.

- Source: [packages/overlays/topics](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/overlays/topics)
- Release note: Accepts SDK StorageDownloader UHRP pages up to 200 rows with deterministic outpoint ordering. Retains selector allowlists and authenticated advertisement admission. Removes serial-DID topic/lookup/storage exports and tm_did/ls_did registrations. Existing BRC189 identity discovery, UORA and all other legitimate topics remain. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 lower bound; clean packed SDK2.8.11 and SDK3 candidate consumers are documented in the identity/DID/VC migration guide. Replaces the tm_mandala/ls_mandala admission, lookup and storage API with Mandala on BRC-162 (BSV-21 binary tokens with authority supply, consuming the @bsv/templates 2.0.0 Bsv21Binary codec): typed MandalaReject refusals with ERR_* codes, the v3 envelope, strict-CBOR admin details committed by the authority output, a trusted-issuer set, an append-only owner journal with inline owner-index repair, and the eviction API. Adds the tm_mandala_registry/ls_mandala_registry identity registry topic (RegistryTopicManager, RegistryLookupService). Changes the persisted Mandala schema (spec section 6.6). UMP lookup requests the retained token-update lineage for presentation, recovery and outpoint queries, within the engine traversal budgets. Adds an SDK4 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 and SDK3 ranges. Requires the repaired SDK4.0.1 hotfix for the SDK4 peer alternative while retaining every existing SDK2/3 alternative and lower bound. Topics2.0.4 removes the fixed KVStore tag-query count cap and pairs with SDK4.1.1 for larger signed token admission and history verification. Other lookup protocols retain their existing count policies.
- Migration: Topics2 is a breaking retirement candidate. Remove DIDTopicManager/createDIDLookupService/DIDRecord/DIDQuery and tm_did/ls_did usage. Resolve immutable identity-key DIDs offline; explicitly configured tm_identity/ls_identity supplies certificate discovery, not DID-document mutation or automatic trust. Preserve existing database/history and plan service rollout without automatic replacement installation. See docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. Mandala is a clean break with no data migration: the old MandalaToken/MandalaAdmin wire format is no longer admitted and 1.x Mandala rows are not read or converted, so start Mandala on a new database with new deploys (existing on-chain outputs are not spent or deleted). MandalaTopicManager drops adminWallet, adminProtocolID and stateStore.isAdminOutpoint and requires trustedIssuers (non-empty compressed lowercase public keys) and engineOutputs, with optional membership, membershipExempt and onOwnerRepair; pass the same MandalaStorageManager (a MandalaStateStore) to admission and lookup. Refusals are MandalaReject { code, reason } from the Reasons catalog; do not match on old error text. MandalaLinkagePayload is replaced by MandalaEnvelope with encodeEnvelope/decodeEnvelope; the register action is replaced by a deploy at output 0 with a deploySig. foldAction, defaultAssetState, AssetAdminState, FoldContext and MandalaTokenRecord use tokenId (<txid>_0) instead of assetId, drop issuerIdentityKey and add feeRatePerKb. Persisted schema (section 6.6): new mandalaOwners and mandalaAuthorities collections; mandalaTokens, mandalaMetadata, mandalaAssetStates and mandalaAdminHistory are keyed by tokenId, metadata holds the decoded deploy payload, and history rows store kind, detailsHex, commitment and delta (plus optional frozenAmount/frozenOwner on freezes). De-trusting an issuer key revokes the authority coins it holds; rotate keys by moving authority coins first. Operators register tm_mandala_registry/ls_mandala_registry explicitly. The infra/overlay-server wiring follows after publication (P1b). The prior 2.0.0 contracts above are the published baseline. This 2.0.1 UMP patch has no API, wire or schema migration; deploy with overlay 2.6.4 to retain history past confirmation. Consumers may keep their current SDK or install @bsv/sdk 4.0.1; no migration is required for this package. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required. To restore larger KVStore tag sets end to end, deploy this package together with SDK4.1.1 and upgrade client SDKs. No KVStore database or token migration is required; preserve all existing tags and signed bytes. Per-tag validation, overall payload/request bounds, signatures, controller binding and pagination are unchanged.

## @bsv/paymail

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/messaging/paymail.md](../packages/messaging/paymail.md)
- Source: [packages/messaging/ts-paymail](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/messaging/ts-paymail)
- Release note: 2.5.1: Refreshes packed Apache-2.0 license, notice, patent and incorporated-material attribution files. The package includes the reviewed Apache-2.0 license, patent notice and incorporated-material notices. Adds BRC-235 public profile lookup (0ace65da5987) and reverse lookup (43dcf83ddc5f): ProfileLookupCapability/ProfileReverseLookupCapability, ProfileLookupRoute/ProfileReverseLookupRoute for hosts, PaymailClient.lookupProfiles/resolveProfile/reverseLookupProfile for clients, and createProfileCertificate/verifyProfileCertificate/checkProfileCertificate for self-signed BRC-52 profile certificates. Every certificate a client reads is verified (type, subject equals certifier, zero revocation outpoint, signature, domain, exact paymail, not released) and at most ten lookup results are processed. A router serving only the two BRC-235 routes, with no requestSenderValidation setting, omits the sender-validation flag from .well-known/bsvalias; every other configuration advertises exactly what it did before. PaymailServerResponseError gains an optional responseStatus set by HttpClient for non-2xx answers. Previous release: Fixes the CommonJS build of the P2P signature and PaymailClient key helpers. The CommonJS build imported @bsv/sdk classes through bundler Node-mode interop, which bound each default import to the whole SDK module, so require() consumers failed at first use with ".default is not a constructor". SDK classes are now imported by name from the SDK barrels; the ESM build, public API and browser bundle size are unchanged. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 lower bound; clean packed SDK2.8.11 and SDK3 candidate consumers are documented in the identity/DID/VC migration guide. Adds an SDK4 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 and SDK3 ranges. Requires the repaired SDK4.0.1 hotfix for the SDK4 peer alternative while retaining every existing SDK2/3 alternative and lower bound.
- Migration: No API, wire or data migration is required. Redistributors must retain the included license and notice files. None. All additions are new exports; existing capabilities, routes, client methods, defaults and discovery documents are unchanged except that a host configured with only the new BRC-235 routes and no requestSenderValidation omits the sender-validation flag. Previous release: None. ESM consumers are unaffected. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. Consumers may keep their current SDK or install @bsv/sdk 4.0.1; no migration is required for this package. SDK4 consumers must use @bsv/sdk >=4.0.1 <5; SDK2/3 consumers retain their existing ranges. No application-wallet wire or data migration is required.
